tasks.objective: Codex runs through an agent-neutral session runner and a registered Codex adapter, reading the final message from piped stdout with no temporary files and no live agent output in the terminal.
completion_criteria: An `AgentAdapter` module for Codex exists under src/agents/ and is registered in one registry that exposes the default agent name and the supported names.

Unit tests show Codex buildArgs yields exec, automatic approval review, the workspace, and -m / reasoning-effort overrides only when supplied, with no output-file option; unsupported settings are silently ignored.
Unit tests show Codex extractFinalMessage returns the stdout text, and reports missing for empty or whitespace-only stdout.

An integration test using a fake codex that writes the final message to stdout shows the run completes, the prompt arrives on the fake's stdin, and the terminal shows only [afk] lines on stderr and nothing on stdout.
An integration test shows no files are left in the temp directory or workspace and no output-last-message argument is passed.
The shared session runner has no Codex-specific code; the fake codex fixture and test helpers no longer use -o.
constraints: The session runner must never select a full-access mode and must keep the existing timeout and signal-escalation behavior.
Adapters stay pure: no state, temp files, or cleanup.
Codex currently receives the prompt as an argument with stdin ignored; per AC-013 and AC-027 it must now read the prompt from stdin (via the - prompt argument).

tasks.objective: Users select the agent with --agent, defaulting to codex, with validation and help driven by the registry.
completion_criteria: Without --agent, every session (including retries) launches the fake codex.
--agent codex is accepted; --agent with an unsupported or empty value prints an option error listing the registry names, exits 2, and launches no session.
--help and -h document --agent <name>, list the registry names, and state the default codex, and still take precedence over an invalid --agent value.
--model and --reasoning-effort values reach the adapter unchanged; with neither, no overrides are passed.
A unit test shows the names accepted by validation and listed in errors and help are exactly the registry keys, with no separate hard-coded list.
constraints: The CLI flag stays --reasoning-effort; only the internal field is named effort.

tasks.objective: A Claude Code adapter drives sessions through print-mode JSON output and its results are classified into the existing execution error kinds.
completion_criteria: With --agent claude, every session in the run, including retries, launches the fake claude and it appears in the --agent error list and help.

A Claude adapter is registered; unit tests show buildArgs selects print mode, JSON output, and the auto permission mode, adds --model / --effort only when supplied, and never contains a full-access permission mode.
Unit tests of extractFinalMessage cover: valid result string, invalid JSON, empty stdout, missing or empty result, and is_error true with a subtype.

Integration tests with a fake claude executable show each row of the AC-008 table maps to the specified execution error, including is_error true on exit 0 and on a non-zero exit with the subtype in the reported reason, and a non-zero exit without structured result reporting only the exit code or signal.
A fake claude run returning a valid protocol result in the JSON result field leads to the same outcomes as Codex (complete, blocked, repeat, fail).
Timeout and Ctrl+C against the fake claude end the run with the same messages, no retry, and the same exit codes as Codex.
constraints: The runner must not parse agent-specific output; the structured error must flow through the adapter's FinalMessageResult (see design).

tasks.objective: Run output is agent-neutral and execution errors are diagnosable from the last 20 lines of the agent's captured stderr.
completion_criteria: Iteration lines read `[afk] Iteration <n>/<max>: starting agent session`; retry, task-failure, execution-error, and final status lines name no specific agent and use the AC-011 wording, with execution errors printed as `[afk] Execution error: …` and blocked runs as `[afk] Run blocked: …`.

Agent stderr is never shown live; a session with an execution error and stderr output prints at most its last 20 stderr lines in original order directly after the execution-error line, including for an error that leads to a retry.
No stderr lines are printed when stderr is empty, or when the session ended with a valid protocol response, a timeout, or an interruption.
The exit-code help text no longer names Codex.
Existing tests are updated to the new wording.
constraints: Wording and tail printing live in shared code (reporter/cli), not in adapters.

tasks.objective: One shared harness behavior suite runs against every registered adapter using a fake executable per agent, proving identical behavior across agents.
completion_criteria: The suite iterates over the registry and covers protocol outcomes, retry policy, iteration limit, timeout, interruption, stderr tail, and output wording for each adapter.
For the same scripted sequence of session results, the Codex and Claude runs produce identical [afk] stderr lines, final status, and exit code.
The Codex fixture emits its final message on stdout and the Claude fixture emits the JSON result object on stdout; no real agent installation is required.
Per-adapter unit tests of buildArgs and extractFinalMessage exist for every registered adapter.
`pnpm test` passes.
constraints: Adding a new registered adapter should require only a fixture and adapter unit tests, not changes to the shared suite's cases.

tasks.objective: Help text, README, and package metadata describe afk as agent-neutral and document each supported agent's prerequisites.
completion_criteria: A help test shows the description and option texts say "the coding agent" instead of Codex and that --model and --reasoning-effort state the value is passed to the agent unchanged.

A README exists that describes afk as agent-neutral, documents --agent, and has a "Supported agents" section with prerequisites, launch mode, and honored harness settings for Codex and Claude Code, as listed in AC-025.
package.json description does not name Codex as the only agent.
constraints: No README exists yet; create one covering the existing CLI surface at a level sufficient to host the new sections.

tasks.objective: Manual smoke checks against the real Codex and Claude Code CLIs are recorded as evidence, with any mismatch captured as follow-up tasks.
completion_criteria: Recorded evidence lists the codex and claude CLI versions used.
Evidence shows `codex exec --approve-for-me -o <file> -` with piped stdout prints the same final message to stdout as to the file, apart from surrounding whitespace.
Evidence shows `afk --agent codex` and `afk --agent claude` each run once in a scratch workspace with a prompt naming no specification or task list, ending in `[afk] Run blocked: …` and exit code 1.
No source files are changed by this task; any mismatch is added to the plan as a follow-up task.
constraints: Manual check, not part of the automated suite. Requires installed and authenticated CLIs; if unavailable, stop and ask the user rather than skipping.
